title: What's new across Microsoft SQL in 2026 so far (SQL Server, Azure SQL, and SQL database in Fabric)
summary: Microsoft's mid-2026 roundup of SQL-family updates spans SQL Server, Azure SQL, and SQL database in Fabric, tagging each item Preview or Generally Available. This source is scoped to only the SQL database in Fabric-relevant items in that roundup, since the rest of the post covers Azure SQL Database and SQL Server items outside the Fabric platform.
audience: Fabric administrators and developers using SQL database in Fabric who want a checkpoint of which cross-SQL capabilities are landing in the Fabric-hosted database engine specifically.
why_it_matters: SQL database in Fabric inherits capabilities from the broader Microsoft SQL engine family on a staggered timeline, so distinguishing what's already shipped for Fabric versus what's still Azure SQL-only (or merely 'coming soon' to Fabric) avoids assuming feature parity that doesn't yet exist.
takeaways: Full collation support and a migration assistant for SQL database in Fabric are both called out as Preview capabilities in this roundup.
Fabric Apps gained support for SQL database as a data source, per this post.

Change Event Streaming, regex-powered Dynamic Data Masking, and local time-zone support are listed as available (or coming) for Hyperscale/SQL Managed Instance first, with SQL database in Fabric explicitly marked as 'coming soon' rather than already available.
The roundup is a curated list of links to individual announcement posts rather than a single deep-dive, so most Fabric-relevant facts here are at a conceptual, what-shipped level.

claims.text: Full collation support for SQL database in Fabric is listed as a Preview capability in this mid-2026 roundup.
A Migration assistant for SQL database in Fabric is listed as a Preview capability, intended to help move existing databases into the Fabric-hosted SQL engine.
Fabric Apps, a Fabric feature for packaging and sharing content, gained support for SQL database as a data source, per this roundup.
Change Event Streaming is listed as available across Hyperscale and SQL Managed Instance, with the post explicitly noting SQL database in Fabric support is coming soon rather than already shipped.
Regex-powered Dynamic Data Masking is listed as a Preview capability coming soon, described in the roundup without a stated Fabric-specific availability date.
Local time zone support is listed as a Preview capability coming soon for Hyperscale, SQL Managed Instance, and SQL database in Fabric together.
